content:
Summer AirPods price cuts are in full swing. While the next generation of earphones may launch as soon as a month from now, at which point prices could drop even further, the AirPods Pro 3 has already hit an all-time low price, the AirPods 4 with Active Noise Cancellation (ANC) has fallen to near its lowest price in six months, and the brand-new AirPods Max 2, which isn't due until 2026, is already $120 off.

Within a month, Apple will very likely officially announce its next-generation in-ear personal listening device, but the company has already upgraded its over-ear headphones earlier this year with the all-new AirPods Max 2, and these new headphones are now selling at an all-time low price.

  • AirPods Pro 3 for $190 (original price $249)
  • AirPods Max 2 for $429 (original price $549)
  • AirPods 4 with Active Noise Cancellation (ANC) for $135 (original price $179) — lowest price in six months
  • AirPods 4 for $99 (original price $129)

Amazon is currently selling the AirPods Max 2 for $429 with shipping, $120 off the original price of $549, one of the best prices ever seen for these headphones since launch. Although a brief $399 deal appeared during Prime Day, stock and color options were quite limited at the time.

Best Buy is currently offering all five colors at discounted prices, part of the 60th anniversary sale that kicked off earlier this morning; Amazon is likely to follow suit shortly.

  • AirPods Max 2 all colors for $429 (original price $549)

Apple has finally delivered a true next-generation upgrade to the AirPods Max earlier this year, though when we'll see a third generation remains unknown. The previous version was regarded by many as AirPods Max 1.5, mainly featuring a new look and USB-C port; but this year's Max 2 brings significant spec improvements, including high dynamic range amplifiers, and a listening experience powered by the Apple H2 chip — active noise cancellation performance improved by up to 1.5x, plus new 'digital signal processing algorithms' to enhance Transparency mode performance.

We've covered all the upgrades in detail before, here's a brief rundown from Apple:

  • Adaptive Audio: Automatically adjusts the intensity of active noise cancellation and Transparency mode based on the user's environment, delivering the optimal listening experience.
  • Conversation Awareness: Automatically lowers media volume and reduces background noise when the user starts talking to someone nearby.
  • Live Translation: Powered by Apple Intelligence, this feature helps users communicate face-to-face in different languages.
  • Voice Isolation: Leveraging advanced computational audio technology driven by the H2 chip, prioritizes capturing the user's voice during calls while blocking out ambient noise.
  • Camera Remote: Users can use the Camera app on iPhone or iPad, or supported third-party camera apps, to remotely take photos or start and stop video recording by pressing the Digital Crown.
  • Studio-Quality Audio Recording: Allows journalists, podcast hosts, singers and other creators to record content with higher audio quality and a more natural vocal texture.
  • Noise Reduction: Helps users avoid exposure to loud environmental sounds while preserving the tonal characteristics of what they're listening to.
  • Personalized Volume: Automatically fine-tunes the listening experience based on the user's long-term preferences.
  • Siri Interactions: Allows users to simply nod for "yes" or shake their head for "no," responding to Siri's prompts easily and privately.
